10rqyo8:2292: In the Claude Code codebase, counting only exact occurrences of KAIROS, it appears 154 times; counting variables prefixed with it, 365 times. What is KAIROS? Simply put, KAIROS is Claude Code's future AI form—an always-on collaborative work partner that shows up at the right moment. KAIROS (καιρός) comes from ancient Greek, meaning 'the right, critical, or opportune moment,' representing a qualitative, beyond-chronological 'timing' or 'crucial instant.' About KAIROS, the point has never been a few extra tool toggles, nor how much product rhetoric like 'resident assistant' or 'proactive work' appears in the docs. What it truly changes is Claude Code's operating paradigm: from a 'synchronous Q&A tool in the terminal' to a 'long-lived, always-on, asynchronously collaborating, cross-channel resident agent that maintains its own working rhythm.' And here is the problem. KAIROS's current repository state is far from 'product freeze.' The peripheral capabilities have grown considerably, but the main loop is not yet fully closed. Bridge, Brief, channel messages, daily memory logs, and background task infrastructure are not PPT slides. Yet the assistant main entry, gate, proactive state, and session discovery are still clearly stubs. What KAIROS rewrites is not features but the operating model. The interaction model of an ordinary CLI is simple: the user opens a terminal, enters a command, the model analyzes context, calls tools, gives an answer, and the process ends. This pattern has a natural ceiling: the AI only exists while the user is looking at the terminal. When the user is away, the system does not work. Incoming external events cannot be handled either. What KAIROS wants to fix is exactly this ceiling. The model it wants: sessions can persist for a long time, after a process restart it can reconnect to the original session, external systems can push messages into the session, and the Agent can keep making progress on tasks even when the user provides no new input. From the current code, KAIROS is already a family of capabilities. Existing sub-features include: KAIROS_BRIEF, KAIROS_CHANNELS, KAIROS_PUSH_NOTIFICATION, KAIROS_GITHUB_WEBHOOKS, KAIROS_DREAM. At the tool registration layer you can see: SleepTool, SendUserFileTool, PushNotificationTool, SubscribePRTool. KAIROS's action set becomes: wait, listen, send back, wake, cross-channel access, continuously maintain context. This shows its positioning is no longer a mere 'local operator'—it is moving toward a 'workflow hub.' Bridge is one of KAIROS's most critical infrastructures. Bridge's data flow: a remote entry receives a user message, pulls work through the bridge, creates or resumes a REPL, the session continues executing, then sends results back. The key point in the code is useReplBridge. In assistant mode, a perpetual bridge session is enabled, so that remote viewers see the same continuous session rather than a new session on every CLI start. But the real closed loop is stuck not in Bridge itself, but in a few key layers: identity detection
